thoughts: Masking words in the decoder helps the model learn to generate refined summaries by forcing it to predict each word based on context from other words, rather than relying on all ground-truth words.

Masking words in the decoder forces the model to predict each word based on context from previously generated or unmasked words, which encourages gradual refinement and prevents direct copying of ground-truth summaries.

Masking words in the decoder forces the model to predict each word sequentially based on context from previously generated words, which enhances the model's ability to generate refined summaries without direct access to ground-truth words.

It first masks each word in the summary draft one by one, then feeds the draft to BERT to generate context vectors. Finally it predicts a refined summary word using an $N$ layer Transformer decoder which is the same as the draft decoder. At t-th time step the n-th word of input summary is masked, and the decoder predicts the n-th refined word given other words of the summary.

retrieved.content: We also conduct experiments on the New York Times(NYT) dataset which also consists of many news articles. The original dataset can be applied here. In our experiment, we follow the dataset splits and other pre-process settings of BIBREF15 . We first filter all samples without a full article text or abstract and then remove all samples with summaries shorter than 50 words. Then we choose the test set based on the date of publication(all examples published after January 1, 2007). The final dataset contains 22,000 training samples and 3,452 test samples and is called NYT50 since all summaries are longer than 50 words.
